title: SpoC-128
blurb: Authenticity of SpoC-128, a NIST Lightweight Cryptography Round-2 candidate. Distinguish real SpoC from a replay-only ideal.

scoring.note: score = log2(budget / advantage^exponent), the security level in bits the attack refutes. Lower is better. No target advantage is fixed: the board measures what a submission proves, because on a new design nobody knows what is reachable.
scoring.exponent_rationale: Decision game: advantage a needs ~a^-2 repetitions to amplify to constant confidence, so q/a^2 is the cost of deciding. Search-flavoured challenges (key recovery, forgery) set 1. No default is baked in; see Micciancio-Walter, On the Bit Security of Cryptographic Primitives.
not_captured: offline work: out of scope by decision — the board scores query complexity, information-theoretically
amplification: q/a^e assumes independent repetition is available
ties are not equivalences: the same bit level can hold very different results

par.source: SpoC-128 key length, NIST LWC Round-2 specification
par.note: Par is the designer's own security claim, not a guess about attack difficulty. Under par is a break of the claim.

baseline.note: Exhaustive key search. Exists for every challenge, so the frontier is never empty.

score_source.note: Declared by the submission, in Lean. The Solution type is indexed by them, so they are part of what is proved; the verifier reads them back with #eval rather than parsing a form.
